zh.text: 模组不再互相顶掉：以前每个模组各自 hook Module.prototype._compile 去改服务端源码，多个模组改同一个文件就只剩一个能生效 —— 先注入的改完内容，后注入的按「整份文件 sha256」校验发现对不上，就安静地放弃（不报错、也没效果）。实测过的那一对是自动挖矿与自动锁定自动集火抢 server/src/network/tcp/handshake.js。现在启动器自带一条注入总线、只注入一条 --require：模组改成向 globalThis.__evejsMods 声明「改哪个文件、加什么、用什么标记」，由总线按 (slot, 注册先后) 串成一条链，每一层看到的是前一层改过之后的内容，带 marker 自动幂等；某一层抛错只跳过它自己、保留上一层结果。顺带解决两件旧毛病：模组清单改走 JSON 文件，模组目录带中文或空格不再让注入失效；NODE_OPTIONS 从 N 条缩成 1 条，装再多模组也不会把它撑爆。老式模组（自己挂钩子）照旧能跑，但只有改用总线的模组才真正彼此共存。

能看见模组到底加载了没有、花了多久：启动主服务器时，服务端输出会给出每个 loader 的就绪 / 失败与毫秒数（[EveJS-MOD] loader 就绪 <模组> 3ms）、全部模组加载完的总耗时（loaders-done total=14 failed=0 ms=1086）、总线补丁的应用情况（<文件> 注入 N 层（A -> B 字节）、<id> 补丁失败，保留上一层结果：<原因>）；每个进程还会把明细写进 _launcher/logs/mod-load-report.json（真服务端进程写总报告，worker / fork 出来的进程各写一份带 pid 的），排查「谁把那个文件改了」直接看它。顺带修掉一个会让报告根本没人写的缺陷：--require 预加载进来的模块里 require.main 永远是空的，入口判定改成回退 process.argv[1]。

模组制作规范（中英双份）里有两处会让人直接踩坑的错：一是写着 require("./src/...") 相对服务端根目录解析，实际相对的是 loader.js 自己的目录，照抄必然 MODULE_NOT_FOUND；二是附录的骨架用了根本不存在的接口（sessionRegistry.list()、s.characterId）。现在路径改成先算 serverRoot，接口换成实测可用的 getSessions() / resolveSessionCharacterID() / chatHub.sendSystemMessage()；「三个必踩的坑」补成四条硬约定，步骤 4 的默认值与生成文件树、排错速查一并改正，并新增附录 G 讲 __evejsMods.register 的四条约定。
模组审核说明不再给固定时长：原先写「人工审核通常需要 30 分钟，通过后自动上架到模组市场」，现按实际流程定为「模组代码审查中，审查时间与模组大小有关，通过后自动上架到模组市场」—— 审查时间本来就随模组体积变化，写死 30 分钟只会让人以为超时了。模组审核条与上架审核横幅两处都换了，含 7 种语言，界面里那个「官方 30 分钟」的常量也一并删掉。
「我创建的」页签里那批上架审核中的模组，每行右侧的「查看版本审核 PR」按钮去掉：那条 PR 由索引仓库托管，审核结论由维护者合并决定，作者盯着 PR 状态没有意义（要查仓库可以直接去 GitHub）。去掉按钮后不再需要回传 PR 状态的入口，连带把只服务于它的 openReview 与 onOpenReview 一并清掉。

en.text: Mods no longer knock each other out. Every loader used to hook Module.prototype._compile and rewrite the server source in memory, so when two mods touched the same file only one of them could take effect: the second one compared the whole file against a sha256 baseline, saw what the first had appended, and quietly gave up (no error, no effect). The pair we measured fighting over server/src/network/tcp/handshake.js was AutoMining and AutoLockFire. The launcher now ships an injection bus and injects a single --require: mods declare "which file, what to add, under which marker" to globalThis.__evejsMods, and the bus chains the declarations by (slot, registration order), so each layer sees what the previous layer produced, with marker-based idempotence. A failing layer only skips itself and the earlier layers survive. Two old headaches go away as well: the plan is read from a JSON file, so mod folders with Chinese characters or spaces no longer break injection, and NODE_OPTIONS shrinks from N entries to one no matter how many mods are installed. Old-style mods that still hook the compiler keep working, but only mods that use the bus really coexist.

You can now see whether mods actually loaded and how long they took. Starting the main server prints each loader's ready / failed state with milliseconds ([EveJS-MOD] loader ready <mod> 3ms), the total for all mods (loaders-done total=14 failed=0 ms=1086) and how the bus patches landed (<file> injected N layers (A -> B bytes), <id> patch failed, keeping earlier layers: <reason>). Every process also writes its detail to _launcher/logs/mod-load-report.json (the real server process writes the summary, worker / forked processes each write one tagged with their pid), which is the first place to look when asking who changed that file. A defect that kept the report from being written at all is fixed too: inside a --require preload require.main is always empty, so the entry check now falls back to process.argv[1].

Two traps in the mod authoring spec (Chinese and English) are fixed. It told authors that require("./src/...") resolves against the server root, while it actually resolves against loader.js's own folder, so copying it always ends in MODULE_NOT_FOUND; and the appendix skeleton used APIs that do not exist (sessionRegistry.list(), s.characterId). The path now computes serverRoot first, and the skeleton uses getSessions() / resolveSessionCharacterID() / chatHub.sendSystemMessage(), which are verified to work. The "three traps" list became four hard rules, the step 4 defaults and the generated file tree were corrected, the troubleshooting table gained MODULE_NOT_FOUND, and a new appendix G documents the __evejsMods.register contract.

The mod review notice no longer promises a fixed duration: "manual review usually takes 30 minutes, then it goes live automatically" is now "mod code is under review, review time depends on mod size, and it goes live on the mod market automatically once approved". Review time really does depend on the size of the mod, and a hard-coded 30 minutes only makes authors think they are overdue. Both the review strip and the review banner were updated in 7 languages, and the hard-coded constant is gone.

The "view version review PR" button on the right of each row in the pending-review list of the "my mods" tab is gone. That PR lives in the index repository and the maintainer decides by merging it, so watching its state from the launcher tells the author nothing; the repository is one click away on GitHub. Removing the button also removed the plumbing that only existed to pass the PR state around (openReview and onOpenReview).
